title: Explainer: China eyes overnight rate as main policy tool, what it means for markets
body: The direct market effect is likely to be modest, because the PBOC is formalising a rate it already targets rather than cutting. The market read so far suggests limited impact, with China's 30-year bond yield slipping only about 1 basis point and the overnight rate steady around 1.26%. The bigger question for traders is whether the new anchor is eventually set near today's overnight level of about 1.25%, below the seven-day rate of 1.40%. Markets could treat that as a mild easing signal, which would tend to support Chinese bonds and weigh slightly on the yuan. For the Australian and New Zealand dollars, which often trade as proxies for China, the framework change matters less than whether it comes with genuine easing that lifts Chinese demand. Oil traders will watch the same thing, given China's role as the world's largest crude importer. --- Separately, coming up later today: China LPR preview: rates seen on hold for a 17th month after Q3 GDP beat --- China's central bank wants to steer its economy with the same short-term lever the Fed uses, and while that is not a rate cut, it changes which numbers traders need to watch. Summary: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said on Monday the central bank will study switching its main policy operations from a seven-day tenor to overnight, when the time is right. The overnight reverse repo rate would replace the seven-day reverse repo rate, the main policy rate since 2024, as the central signal for monetary policy.

title: Goldman Sachs sees $25 war risk premium in Brent, forecasts $90 in December and $80 in 2027
body: Goldman's estimate implies Brent is trading well above where supply and demand alone would put it, which leaves prices vulnerable to a sharp drop if the risk of escalation fades, and exposed to further spikes if the conflict widens. The forecast path points lower over time, with the bank expecting a shift into surplus from the fourth quarter to pull prices back toward $80 in 2027, a level consistent with UBS's view that Brent will approach $80 next summer. Near-term support is likely to come from depleted inventories, including a US Strategic Petroleum Reserve at its lowest since 1982, and from investors using oil as a hedge for their stock and bond holdings. For inflation-sensitive markets, a fading premium would ease pressure on central banks and bond yields, while a renewed spike would reinforce the hawkish case. --- Earlier: US strategic oil reserve falls to lowest since 1982 as Iran war release drains stocks --- Goldman Sachs reckons about $25 of every barrel of Brent is a bet on the Iran war getting worse, and if that bet does not pay off, the bank sees prices drifting back toward $80. title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6813 – Reuters estimate
body: The fixing mechanism matters most right now because its message has shifted over the past month. For nearly a year, the PBOC has set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, which traders read as an effort to slow the yuan's appreciation, and in late August that gap reached its widest since February, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high. Through September, however, the midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the central bank has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The fixing is still set weaker than models imply, so this looks like a loosening of the brakes rather than their removal. The balance Beijing is weighing is unchanged: a firmer currency supports capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness while the domestic economy remains soft. The gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest guides to how far the PBOC is willing to let the yuan run.--- The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and after months of saying slow down, it has lately been saying go, gradually.Summary: The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets.

title: The Hormuz shipping attacks nobody is counting: inside the US Navy's go-dark guidance
body: Hormuz attack counts are a floor, and a US Navy FAQ may help explain why The official tally of attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is incomplete, and the body that compiles it says so. In its weekly overview on 16 October, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) said it was struggling to establish the true number of attacks because the majority of vessels targeted were refusing to report to it. It recorded 12 attacks that week, ten of them inside the Strait, with one vessel lost. It added that it knew of further incidents through other sources but could not include them without verification. For oil traders, that matters more than any single weekly figure. Freight rates, war-risk premium s and assessments of supply risk all lean on these counts. If most attacked ships are staying silent, the published number is a minimum, not a measure. Why ships might stay silent Shipowners have obvious commercial reasons to keep quiet, including insurance complications, exposure with their flag state and sensitivity about routing. But a less noticed document may also be part of the picture. A US Navy FAQ for shipping companies, highlighted in a post on X by the account @angertab, sets out how the Navy supports transits on the southern route through the Strait. It was issued by the Naval Cooperation and Guidance for Shipping (NCAGS) cell at US Naval Forces Central Command (NAVCENT), the unit that liaises with merchant ships.

title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin to Ethereum mainnet: what changes, and what it means for ETH
body: JPMorgan Chase has extended JPM Coin (ticker JPMD), its US dollar deposit token, to the Ethereum mainnet. Approved institutional clients now have a second public network for moving dollars around the clock. Bloomberg reported the move on Monday, 19 October, citing the bank, and the Ethereum Foundation flagged it the same day. JPMD has run on Base, Coinbase's Ethereum layer-2 network, since November 2025, and Base remains in service. The move is a meaningful step for Ethereum as financial infrastructure. It is not, on current evidence, a new source of demand for ether. JPMD also remains closed to everyone except approved JPMorgan clients. What JPM Coin actually is JPMD is a deposit token: each unit represents one US dollar that a client holds at JPMorgan. That makes it different from a stablecoin such as USDC, which is issued by a non-bank company and backed by reserves held elsewhere. A deposit token is a claim on the bank itself. In effect, it is ordinary commercial bank money moved onto a blockchain. The practical gain is timing. A transfer that would normally wait on banking hours and business-day settlement can complete almost instantly, at any hour, including weekends. Why mainnet, when Base was cheaper Base was promoted on sub-cent fees, and transactions on Ethereum mainnet typically cost more. So the move is not about saving money. Kinexys, JPMorgan's blockchain unit, said it chose Ethereum because so much liquidity and so many tokenized assets already sit there.

title: German producer prices hit highest since March 2023 as energy costs soar, fueling inflation worries

Looking at the monthly breakdown, energy prices rose by 5.8% in September compared to the month before. So, much of the headline increase can be attributed to that. And therein lies the worry for consumer prices too, as higher producer prices will eventually trickle down the chain and raise broader inflation pressures in Germany. In turn, that will keep the ECB in a rather uncomfortable spot amid flagging growth conditions and fiscal worries alongside stubborn inflation. title: Macro pulse: France's debt crisis doesn't have to get worse to keep hurting the euro
body: France has been the talk of the town in Europe over the past few weeks, and even more so after the weekend riots that we have just seen. Perhaps the only good news is that we haven't quite seen France's debt troubles spiral into a full-blown crisis. But even if things stay exactly as they are, I would argue that France's problems are still a big risk for the euro. The French-German 10-year yield spread has widened again to around 147 bps as of yesterday, as investors continue to demand a much higher premium to hold French government debt. Now, that is still just below the key 150 bps threshold from the highs earlier this month. So, it's not to say that the latest developments are leading to another euro area debt crisis just yet. Having said that, I wouldn't label the yield spread at the current level as being reassuring either. France's borrowing costs are already on the verge of hitting 5%, while Germany's are closer to 3.5%. And with France struggling to get its budget deficit under control, there's little reason for investors to suddenly stop demanding that extra premium. And that is where the euro might be facing a problem. Even if France's fiscal troubles don't escalate into a wider euro area debt crisis, persistently elevated borrowing costs can still do plenty of damage. If things keep up, it means that France will have to spend more on servicing its debt as existing bonds mature and are refinanced.

A hold at the 29-30 October meeting, paired with an upgraded inflation assessment, would keep a December hike in play and could lift short-dated Japanese government bond yields. Oil is a key swing factor: Daiwa notes import prices have started rising again on higher crude, and any further jump in oil linked to the Iran war would add to the risk of inflation overshooting, strengthening the case for faster tightening. For Japanese equities, gradual hikes alongside solid capital spending are unlikely to derail the market, though a faster pace would test valuations. Long-dated JGBs, where yields have already risen above 3%, remain sensitive to any shift in the BOJ's tone. - After decades of trying to get inflation up to 2%, the Bank of Japan's new problem is making sure it stays there, and Daiwa says the answer will be found in next spring's pay packets. title: PBOC to run daily overnight reverse repos to Nov 2 in first step after policy rate signal
body: The direct effect should be calmer overnight funding in China's interbank market through month-end, with the 1 trillion yuan daily cap large enough to stop short-term rates spiking. The bigger market question is the rate the operations carry, which has not been confirmed. If it is set near the current overnight market level of around 1.25%, below the seven-day policy rate of 1.40%, traders may read it as a preview of a lower policy anchor, which would tend to support Chinese government bonds and could weigh on the yuan. If it is set at the top of the existing corridor, it would mainly act as a ceiling and carry little policy signal. For the Australian and New Zealand dollars and for oil, the operations matter only if they turn out to be the first step toward genuine easing that lifts Chinese demand. --- A day after saying it would study an overnight policy rate, China's central bank has started using one every day, but until it reveals the price, markets cannot tell whether this is a dress rehearsal or a month-end safety net. Summary: The People's Bank of China will conduct overnight reverse repo operations daily from 21 October to 2 November. The operations will use fixed-rate, quantity-based tenders, capped at 1 trillion yuan a day. Foreign-invested banks that act as RMB settlement banks will be eligible counterparties. The move follows Governor Pan Gongsheng's comments on Monday that the PBOC will study making the overnight rate its main policy rate.

title: Beyond Data: Why Context is the Next Frontier in Trading AI
body: Two traders can receive the same market signal and reach different decisions. One may be considering a new position; the other may already have substantial exposure to the same instrument. This was the central point I explored at iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong. As artificial intelligence (AI) needs to consider a trader's circumstances alongside market data. From Trading Signals to Contextual Intelligence Machine-learning models can analyse historical market data to identify patterns that might offer trading opportunities. A signal based on historical prices does not, by itself, account for a trader's open positions. If it suggests buying EUR/USD (Euro against the US Dollar), someone already holding a large buy position would need to check whether adding to it fits their risk limits. Contextual intelligence looks at how three types of information interact when traders make decisions. • Personal context covers the trader's strategy, capital, trading habits, and risk tolerance. • Market context includes economic developments, volatility, and liquidity, or how easily an instrument can be traded. • Trade context concerns the position itself, including its size, intended holding period, and stop-loss and take-profit levels. If market volatility rises while a trader holds an open position, the range of potential gains and losses may widen. Whether this calls for an adjustment depends on the position's size and direction, the trader's strategy, and their risk limits.

title: Germany October ZEW survey current conditions -35.9 vs -45.0 expected
body: Germany October ZEW survey current conditions -35.9 vs -45.0 expected Prior -47.1 Germany October ZEW survey economic sentiment 28.1 vs 30.0 expected Prior 34.7 The breakdownIt's a mixed showing as the current conditions index shows a marked improvement but the expectations/outlook index falls further in October. The latter is the softest reading since July and marks a turn in optimism towards the German economy in the coming six months. ZEW notes that while the headline measure might have improved, private consumption and investment are still weak amid higher energy prices. And while the economy as a whole is slowly emerging from stagnation, the recovery itself is still "not self-sustaining". The readings here will do little to convince of better times up ahead for the euro area economy, not least with French fiscal risks and a more dicey bond market backdrop to deal with currently. What does the data measure?The ZEW survey measures financial analysts' and institutional investors' views on Germany's economy. The expectations index looks six months ahead, while the current conditions index assesses the present economic situation. Why does it matter to markets?Germany is Europe's largest economy, so changes in confidence can offer an early indication of where Eurozone growth may be heading. Markets will be watching whether forward-looking optimism holds up or starts to deteriorate.
